title: Choose runtime-async compilation deliberately (experimental)
goal: Choose experimental runtime-async code generation when upgrading, and distinguish live diagnostics from failure stacks and removed runtime switches.

selectionNotes: Experimental CoreCLR compiler flag. Public RC2 SDK requires Features; UseRuntimeAsync alone was inert.

prerequisites: Use the complete offline source/configuration and verify the consumer matches this route.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Use the .NET 11 SDK C# compiler and its explicit runtime-async feature flag.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: This verified edition targets net11.0; the .NET 10 sample is a comparison, not an older-target catalogue route.

language.name: C#
language.reason: The public RC2 compiler accepts the explicit feature under C# 15; no preview-language opt-in is required.

stabilityLimitations: Actual RC2 evidence; final GA reconciliation is separate.
constraints: Rebuild the intended assembly; removed runtime variables cannot change emitted methods. Live stacks and exception stacks are different evidence.
